item.text: The initial read returned `not_found`; I initialized the project from your supplied snapshot. The claims support TXU0304 as the preferred family candidate for standard SPI’s three-forward, one-return topology. Direct 3.3 V drive exceeds the stated DUT pin limit, and one SN74AXC4T245 cannot provide that direction split. Package selection, electrical and timing budgets, supply implementation, and physical validation remain open.

actions.description: Capture actual DUT marking, package and suffix; reconcile to package-specific manufacturer pinout. Identify exact programmer and obtain its guaranteed interface and timing specifications. Select exact TXU0304 orderable package, footprint, availability and assembly constraints.
Complete worst-case logic-level, load and SPI timing budgets from additional traceable evidence; choose SPI mode and maximum clock only when supported.

Specify local 1.8 V regulator implementation, current and tolerance budget, decoupling, sequencing, protection, common return and OE bias/control. Resolve unused DUT pins and inactive CS behavior from exact device documentation; review partial-power/backfeed behavior.
Produce schematic and package-verified footprints, run ERC, then PCB/DRC and independent design review. Preserve unresolved findings and physical authority gates.

Prepare a separately authorized bench validation procedure for identity/continuity, supply/load/transients, OE/sequencing, logic margins and SPI timing. Record actual measurements with traceability when authorized; this plan performs no fabrication or power-on and supplies no bench evidence.

architecture_candidates.rationale: Declared 3.3 V host drive exceeds VCC+0.4 V: 2.2 V at the 1.8 V target and at most 2.35 V across the stated DUT operating range. Absolute maxima are stress limits, not valid logic operating targets. Direct 3.3 V supply also exceeds 1.95 V.
Three A-to-B channels and one B-to-A channel match standard SPI. Both proposed rails lie within stated supply ranges; this alone does not establish logic or timing compatibility.

Two shared-direction two-channel groups allow 4+0, 2+2, or 0+4 directions, not simultaneous 3+1 across four signals. Supply ranges include targets but do not cure topology mismatch. Rejection is scoped to one device implementing all four channels; additional devices would require a separate design.

decisions.statement: Adopt the proposed TXU0304 logical mapping for further review only. No package pin numbers or physical DUT identity are inferred; dual/quad SPI is outside this fixed-direction proposal.

Retain default power off. Design for OE low to disable outputs; biasing, rail reference, startup, shutdown, partial-power behavior, and protection remain unverified. High impedance is not evidence of safe power sequencing.
Use component pin and supply claims for the conditional candidate; the SPI application illustration is not a component guarantee or design validation.

requirements.statement: Design and verify DUT supply remains 1.7–1.95 V, including tolerance, ripple, transient and load effects. Maintain all pins within specified operating limits; -0.6 V to VCC+0.4 V is only the supplied absolute-maximum envelope.
Resolve marking, suffix and package before assigning DUT pins or footprint; select exact translator orderable package and validate its pinout.

Obtain guaranteed VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL, output loading and delay limits at selected rails and conditions. Budget host-to-DUT clock/data/CS and DUT-to-host return delay, skew, setup/hold and programmer sampling for a justified SPI clock. No clock rate is approved.

Three A-to-B channels and one B-to-A channel match standard SPI. Both proposed rails lie within stated supply ranges; this alone does not establish logic or timing compatibility.

Two shared-direction two-channel groups allow 4+0, 2+2, or 0+4 directions, not simultaneous 3+1 across four signals. Supply ranges include targets but do not cure topology mismatch. Rejection is scoped to one device implementing all four channels; additional devices would require a separate design.

blockers: Exact physical DUT marking, package, orderable suffix, and package-specific pinout.
Exact programmer identity, voltage levels under load, supported clock rate, and timing behavior.
Selected TXU0304 orderable package, footprint, availability, and assembly constraints.
Complete VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL and propagation-delay timing budget at the selected supplies and load.
Local 1.8 V supply implementation, current budget, sequencing, decoupling, protection, and OE behavior.
Schematic/ERC/PCB/DRC results and all physical measurements.
assessment.scope: Conditional standard-SPI family architecture only; full machine plan unsupported by available design and physical evidence.
assessment.source_conflict_assessment: No contradictory claims identified in the supplied snapshot. Hash identity does not establish authenticity, currentness, or physical identity.
tool_failures: Initial canonical project GET returned 404 not_found; supplied snapshot bootstrapped per manifest.

decisions.statement: Adopt the proposed TXU0304 logical mapping for further review only. No package pin numbers or physical DUT identity are inferred; dual/quad SPI is outside this fixed-direction proposal.

Retain default power off. Design for OE low to disable outputs; biasing, rail reference, startup, shutdown, partial-power behavior, and protection remain unverified. High impedance is not evidence of safe power sequencing.
Use component pin and supply claims for the conditional candidate; the SPI application illustration is not a component guarantee or design validation.

requirements.statement: Design and verify DUT supply remains 1.7–1.95 V, including tolerance, ripple, transient and load effects. Maintain all pins within specified operating limits; -0.6 V to VCC+0.4 V is only the supplied absolute-maximum envelope.
Resolve marking, suffix and package before assigning DUT pins or footprint; select exact translator orderable package and validate its pinout.

Obtain guaranteed VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL, output loading and delay limits at selected rails and conditions. Budget host-to-DUT clock/data/CS and DUT-to-host return delay, skew, setup/hold and programmer sampling for a justified SPI clock. No clock rate is approved.
